pages.title: Photosynthesis
pages.extract: Photosynthesis is a system of biological processes by which photosynthetic organisms, such as most plants, algae, and cyanobacteria, convert light energy, typically from sunlight, into the chemical energy necessary to fuel their metabolism. Photosynthesis usually refers to oxygenic photosynthesis, a process that produces oxygen.

pages.title: Chlorophyll
pages.extract: Chlorophyll is any of several related green pigments found in cyanobacteria and in the chloroplasts of algae and plants. It allows plants to absorb energy from light.

pages.title: Photosynthesis (disambiguation)
pages.extract: Photosynthesis may refer to: the biological process; a 1987 album.

pages.title: Calvin cycle
pages.extract: The Calvin cycle is the light-independent stage of photosynthesis in which carbon dioxide is turned into glucose.

pages.title: Leaf
pages.extract: A leaf is a principal appendage of the stem of a vascular plant, usually borne laterally above ground and specialized for photosynthesis.
